fuzz.why_not_cargo_fuzz: cargo-fuzz is not installed and cannot be fetched (cargo --offline, no network); the crate is not in the local registry.
fuzz.limitation: Deterministic structured mutation, not coverage-guided. It finds panics, OOB and invariant violations reachable from its mutation set; it does not explore the path set libFuzzer's feedback loop would. Recorded as DR-4.
properties_asserted: no panic on any input (catch_unwind around every entry point)
write ∘ parse = id in lenient mode
every chunk but the last ends on a record boundary
fuzz.defects_note: Both were CRLF round-trip defects in the shared parser/writer; see DR-5. Neither input is accepted by cutadapt or UMI-tools, which is why no oracle suite could have found them.

design_deviations.title: rust-umitools keeps extension-based gzip detection
design_deviations.reason: The shared crate sniffs content; rust-umitools has always opened .gz inputs as gzip and plain inputs as plain. The two differ only when a file's name and content disagree. Changing it would be an observable change on input the oracle does not cover, so it was left alone and pinned by a test.
design_deviations.reversible: one-line change plus an oracle case; listed for W1-3

design_deviations.title: bioinfo-fastx uses xz2 + lzma-sys, not liblzma
design_deviations.reason: Cargo permits one package per links value; rust-htslib already provides links="lzma" through lzma-sys, so the liblzma form would make the workspace unresolvable. W1-1 measured byte-identical xz output (DR-2 there); this crate's round-trip tests re-assert it.
design_deviations.dependency_set: the plan's crate table names flate2, bzip2, liblzma, zstd; liblzma is realised as xz2+lzma-sys for the links reason

design_deviations.title: BGZF MTIME is zero
design_deviations.reason: Reference BGZF writers stamp the current time; this one writes zero so output is reproducible and a fixture can pin it. No reader depends on MTIME. Deliberate byte difference from htslib's output.

design_deviations.title: the fuzz corpus is an in-repo harness, not cargo-fuzz/libFuzzer
design_deviations.reason: cargo-fuzz is not installed and cannot be fetched offline; the crate is not in the local registry. Rather than claim a run that did not happen, an in-repo deterministic harness was written and run for the required 600 s.
design_deviations.limitation: Not coverage-guided: it will not reach the path set libFuzzer's feedback loop would.
design_deviations.real_fix: add cargo-fuzz with a persistent corpus in CI (needs nightly + network at build time); listed for W1-3/W1-6

design_deviations.title: two genuine defects found by fuzzing and fixed
design_deviations.introduced_by: this step (the shared parser/writer did not exist before)
design_deviations.detail: An embedded carriage return could not round-trip: the parser strips one trailing \r per line, so a line ending in two carriage returns parsed successfully with a \r left inside the field, and writing it back produced a line that re-parsed differently. Affected the separator and quality lines first, then the header. Fixed by rejecting an embedded \r in the header, sequence, separator and quality lines, with a clear message; the writer also strips a trailing \r defensively.
design_deviations.why_oracles_missed_it: Neither input is valid FASTQ, so neither cutadapt 4.6 nor UMI-tools 1.1.6 accepts it; no oracle case covers it.
design_deviations.regression_tests_added: parser-level tests plus the fuzz harness's write∘parse identity property

design_deviations.title: a property the fuzz harness deliberately does not assert
design_deviations.reason: The harness first asserted that chunked parsing finds the same record count as a single pass. That is false for malformed input, and correctly so: a chunk boundary can fall where the whole-input parser would have kept reading. It was replaced with the two properties that are true and useful: chunks tile the input exactly, and every chunk but the last ends on a record boundary. Pipeline determinism holds for valid input, which is what the gate and the differential suites verify.
